From playtest 0001 (`docs/playtest/0001-commander-seat.md`, response in `docs/playtest/0001-response.md`). This is the session's summary judgement on the seat, in his own words:

> reported UI issues limit enjoyment for human commander right now. I issue orders and get little feedback on anything after that until either an Objective changes hands (which could do with a notification like you get in singleplayer when your objectives are satisfied/changes) or a squad is silently wiped (which again could use a notification).

## What exists today

`cti_fnc_mapRender` redraws markers and a hint on every Observation push, and `cti_lastJudgementText` carries the port's answer to the last Command. Both are *state*, and both are only visible with the map open. Nothing in the client announces an *event*.

So the two moments that actually change the Commander's situation — ground changing hands, and a Squad ceasing to exist — arrive as a silent difference in a picture he may not be looking at, five seconds late, and in the wiped case as an absence he cannot distinguish from a Squad on the march (#175).

## What to build

An event notification channel for the Commander, in the shape Arma's own singleplayer task notifications take. Both events are already known server-side — ownership is tracked for the win conditions, and the daemon counts Squad strength — so this is a push and a presentation, not new bookkeeping.

Two events to start:

- an Objective or Base changing hands, either way, named and with the new owner;
- one of this Commander's own Squads reaching zero.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both events raise a notification on the owning Commander's client, visible without the map open.
- The events reach the client through the existing Observation/Effect path rather than a new remoteExec target — the mode=1 whitelist does not grow (#18's constraint, and it holds for anything the client receives as well as anything it sends).
- The AI Commander is unaffected: a notification is a presentation of a fact the Observation already carries, so nothing about the planner's inputs changes. If it turns out a notification needs a fact the wire does not have, that is the same decision as #175 and belongs there.
- An in-world probe asserts both notifications fire: stage an ownership flip and a Squad wipe, and assert the client-side notification, not merely the server-side event.

## Note for the ubiquitous language

CONTEXT.md has no term for a Squad reduced to zero. The response says "wiped"; the code says `size: 0`. Noted for `/domain-modeling` rather than settled here.
